utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is the Defence ready to continue cross-examination of the witness? The Chamber has received two new documents, 31A and B, to be put in the brown or in the yellow binder?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In the brown binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the brown binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And may I indicate as well, during the cross-examination of this witness, I am likely to refer to a forensic report served by the Prosecution in French at the back end of last week. We are having copies of the French made available. There is no English translation available, but the content of the passages which I would wish to put to this witness are tolerably clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber is further able to orient itself in the French language as well, so it should not ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have a few brief preliminary comments. I did what was necessary so that the translations of the missing legends in document 64 be done, and as for annex 65 there was the issue of the missing photographs that you pointed out quite legitimately. The document is not available. In fact, we don't have that page, and that's why it is not in the annex. It's not that it was forgotten. It was simply because the Prosecution does not have that. The Evidence Unit doesn't have that document. Thirdly, as regards the forensic report that Mr. Emmerson has just referred to. The translation is underway and has not been finished as of yet. And the last point regarding a future witness, Professor Dunjic, who will be available tomorrow, and the annexes will be in the e-court system so that we will be ready for the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for the update, Mr. Dutertre. One other matter, there was a witness who would have to appear today. The latest information is that the witness finally received the message that he was expected today but that he's unable to come today. That's the latest message that the Chamber received. So, in scheduling, we don't have to consider anymore the possibility that he would appear. Then, Mr. Avramovic, may I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Emmerson will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Emmerson, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I want to start, if I may, this morning, Mr. Avramovic, by asking you some questions about the dates and documentation that you were responsible for in relation to what you claim to have been the first visit to the canal. Could you start, please, by looking at paragraph 44 of your consolidated witness statement, which is I believe tab 15 in the yellow bundle. You will need both the yellow and the brown file. Now, at paragraph 44, you are recorded as having written, and this is a statement very recently signed by you, in June of this year: "I think we arrived at the Lake Radonjic canal area around noon. I think it was on the 9th of September, 1998. I'm quite sure it was on the 9th of September, 1998." What was it that made you sure that it was the 9th of September that you arrived?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The video footage that was shown to me at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it was purely the date on the video, was it, that caused you to indicate that it was the 9th of September?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we then turn to paragraph 50, please, where you refer to annex 14 to your witness statement, which is a photograph album, and you'll find that photograph album behind tab 26 in the brown folder. Perhaps you could take that for a moment. Now, you say in your witness statement that this photograph album was compiled by your colleagues and yourself. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we look for your purposes the first two pages of the Serbian text, and for the Trial Chamber and those of us following in the English they are translated at 26b, we can see that these documents bear the date of the 8th of September. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Why does -- do these documents bear that date?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were referring to the scene of crime investigation record that we made. And it was later on that we realised that the date was wrong, and I explained that in my statement. All the documents we produced bear that date because we were referring back to that. That's why we have the date of the 8th.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. You were referring back to the scenes of crimes register to remind you the date upon which you should be recording dates in the documentation you created. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not really a register. It's a book of records of all the scenes of crime we attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But this photograph album was compiled long after the 8th of September, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly, one month later --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- two months at most. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So you compile an album of photographs two months later, between one and two months later, and then date the document the 8th of September, back-dating it by reference to a crime scene register. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then at paragraph 51 of your witness statement, you refer to this album of photographs; and based on that. You say: "There could be a mistake on the video, and I am unsure if we visited the scene on the 9th, or rather, the 8th." Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, since the -- the time to which the video-recorder was set was wrong, that led me to my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Leaving the time on the video-recorder out of the equation for a moment, what you tell us in paragraph 51 is that by reference to the date that appears on this album of photographs and by reference to the date that appears on another document you compiled in -- or another document that was compiled in relation to the finding of bullet casings, you have come to believe that the date of the visit may have been the 8th and not the 9th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And yet you tell us that the date of the 8th here is a date that was taken from an error in the crime scene register. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So based on an erroneous entry in the crime scene register, the date of the 8th appears on the documentation; and you then take that date as a basis for saying you may be mistaken in relation to the date of your visit. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but we noticed that error only recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that, and that is a function, I suggest, of the fact that these documents were created in order to suggest that the canal scene was discovered on the 8th, when, in fact, it was not?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we then look at paragraph 52 of your witness statement and have some clarification of that, please. Paragraph 52 reads as follows: "After having reviewed the register of crime scene investigations of SUP Djakovica in Jagodina on the 31st of May, 2007, I noticed that there was something illogical about the date of the crime scene investigation at Lake Radonjic. "The two preceding investigations are entered into the register as taking place on the 9th of September, 1998, and then the Lake Radonjic investigation is entered as taking place on the 8th of September, 1998, which is probably a mistake and the reason we subsequently used this date in our forensic reports as a reference point." You see that in paragraph 52 of your witness statement?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now let me see if I've understood this correctly. On the 31st of May of this year, just a little over a month ago, you consulted a document in Jagodina at the SUP Djakovica office. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you know that that document has been requested, do you, by the Defence and Prosecution for production?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that. I didn't know that this particular document was requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the document was not requested from this particular witness, but rather the Serb authorities because they are the owners, so to speak, of the document. But it's not up to -- it was not requested from the witness as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But if Mr. Emmerson asks questions about it, it could be that he knows something about it. But his answer is that he didn't know. You say you didn't know. Do you know by now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me be clear. You looked at this document, and help me to make sure I've understood the position correctly. There were three entries you focused on. And in order as they appeared in the book, there were two that were dated the 9th; and then entered into the back after those two, there was one dated the 8th. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the one following it was entered under the date of the 10th of September, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So that we're clear, there is an entry for the 9th, then another entry for the 9th, then the Lake Radonjic entry for the 8th, and then a further entry for the 10th. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This shows that there was an error most probably there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And the reason you say there must have been an error, and that it is illogical, is that because if these entries had been entered in the correct order, you would expect to find an entry relating to the 8th to be before any entries relating to the 9th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the register has entries in a chronological order.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so. And they're entered as the investigation is opened. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So they're entered at the same time as in contemporaneously with the opening of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon return from a scene of crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the illogicality that you perceived in this register led you to conclude that the date of the 8th was an error. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that the correct date should have been the 9th if this was a genuine record?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The register is genuine, and it should have had 9th as the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that would mean, based on that inference, Mr. Avramovic, that your testimony is that the visit to the canal must have happened on the 9th, and that all of the records you completed which refer to it starting on the 8th are inaccurate because of this error in the crime scene register. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection to that question because it calls for speculation on the part of the witness, who explains in paragraph 52 that it is most likely an error. He does not say that it's certain. He's being asked to speculate on various dates, and I believe he should not have to answer those questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, he has answered the questions meanwhile, Mr. Dutertre. And, of course, he spontaneous -- yes. Mr. Emmerson, of course, taking the witness to certain explanation of the error --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: His own explanation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, of course, you are leading him a bit there as well. To some extent, it's his own explanation. To what extent it's logical. If an 8 appears after two times after 9, it could be that the 8 is wrong. It could be that the two times 9 are wrong, that they should have been 8s. Well, there are several explanations possible, not this one to be the necessary and logical -- and, of course, one of the things is the whole line of questioning - it came into my mind but Judge Hoepfel reminds me of that - of course, you are talking about genuine records. Sometimes people forget to make an entry into a register and do it not in the chronological -- I take it you are aware that all these thoughts --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Come into our minds. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want then to understand your final position on this, Mr. Avramovic. Are you saying that the journey to the canal that you took part in was on the 8th or the 9th or that you just don't know?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was on the 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Can you say why you believe that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on all the other documents that I saw subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And which documents are they that you saw that referred to it as being the 9th?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Various documents. A request by the judge to engage a group of forensic experts and things like that. I can't remember which documents those are, but they fall in nicely with the chronology of the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So you've reviewed a number of documents, have you, that bear the date of the 9th as relating to the date of the first visit. Is that correct? Have I understood your evidence correctly?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know when the first day was, when the second day was, who went to the site for the on-site inspection; and based on all that, I concluded that it was on the 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see. Thank you. Now, with that in mind, I want to ask you, please, one or two questions about the route that was taken to the canal. First of all, can you confirm, please, that the route that you took on the first day, whenever it was, was via Donji Bites and Shaptej?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And from Shaptej to the canal, how did you travel?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By vehicles from Saptej to the Ekonomija; and then from the Ekonomija to the canal, we went on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you didn't, for example, drive through the village of Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You went over land, across dirt tracks, did you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was there any physical difficulty for you and the other Serbian forces to make your way from Donji Bites over land to the canal?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Save for the bad road, there were no other obstacles.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's perfectly possible for Serbian officials to get to the canal area from Donji Bites. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you saw, is it correct, VJ forces positioned at Donji Bites?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe I saw them somewhere around Donji Bites.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were there MUP forces stationed in that area as well?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: With the VJ?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you whether they were together.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, from what you saw, were they in separate positions or were they in the same position geographically?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I can't remember whether they were together.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There had been VJ and MUP forces stationed in that area around Bites for some considerable number of months, had there not?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure that they had been there already for a number of months before.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I be clear, is it right then that on the route that you took you drove your vehicles all the way up to the economic farm?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And from the economic farm, you walked to the canal?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Bekim Kalamashi, Zenelj Alija were leading the way. They went in front of us, and that's the route that they took to lead us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And at any point before you got to the economic farm, did you and your colleagues dismount from the vehicles?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It wasn't safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At any point en route to the canal, did you and your colleagues come under hostile fire?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was there ever an occasion when a mortar or mortars were shot at your group en route to the canal?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was there ever an occasion when there was an exchange of fire between the MUP officers who were accompanying you and the KLA or others who were firing upon you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no resistance at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just to be absolutely clear about it, we have heard a suggestion in this case from two witnesses, one who claims to have been there and one who reports what he was told, that en route to the canal the group with which you were travelling was attacked, that there was an exchange of fire, and on one account that there was a two-hour delay whilst reinforcements had to arrive. None of that is true, Mr. Avramovic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was there any firing at the canal? Was there any shooting at the canal whilst you were there on the first day you attended?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could hear gun-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Whilst you were there at the canal?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And where was that gun-fire coming from?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From various directions. It's very difficult for me to remember where from exactly. One could hear gun-shots from all over the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I want to ask you now, please, about paragraph 45 of your witness statement, and if you could have a look at that and also at paragraph 57. In paragraph 57, you refer to the fact that when you arrived there, there were a few bodies floating in the canal which seemed to have been killed recently. Can you give us an indication of how many bodies you saw floating in the canal, first of all?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I believe that there were two.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And, at paragraph 45, you say that by the second day they had been washed away. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the course of that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you can be clear, can you, that when you attended on the second day, whenever that was, those bodies had gone?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It had been raining, the water was high, and it washed them away.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you ever see those two bodies being recovered from the canal at all during the times that you were there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be sure of that, but they should be among the bodies that were found subsequently in the canyon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. They should be, and my suggestion is that they are not. And the question I'm asking you is whether you ever saw them being removed?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't say that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you ever see them again anywhere after the first day?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You used the word "removed," whether you ever saw them being removed. It's unclear whether you mean removed from the concrete part of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or from any other place. It could create confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I ought to clarify that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you ever see those two bodies being taken out of the water, either in the concrete section of the canal or lower down in the canyon?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that they were removed from the canyon because the water washed them away into the other part of that canal, to the natural canal, to the canyon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that that is the account that you are purporting to give to the Trial Chamber. The question was: Did you ever see them yourself being removed from either the concrete section or from the canyon?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from the concrete section, and most probably the bodies were recovered in the canyon. I'm almost sure of that. I did not see them having been removed from the concrete part of the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see them being taken out of the canyon, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object. The witness has said he doesn't know. The same question has repeated several times. I don't see what the witness can add to his previous answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact, I think the witness can. But, Mr. Emmerson, perhaps you should put the question in a different way. The logical sequence of questions would be, where the witness now has testified that he did not see these bodies, which as far as the evidence goes until now were the only bodies in the concrete section of the canal, that logical sequence would be: Have you seen bodies taken from the canyon? Have you verified at any time whether these bodies were the same as you saw before in the concrete canal. And then, finally, if that gets affirmative answer, how the verification was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that's the logical --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You heard Judge Orie's questions. Let me put them to you in order. First of all, did you see bodies being removed from the canyon section?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see any body that you believed to have been those two bodies that had previously been floating in the concrete section of the canal, did you see those bodies removed from the canyon yourself?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember exactly. I can't assert anything with any degree of certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. And finally this: Did you ever see them yourself in the canyon section?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There were a lot of bodies, so I can't be sure that any of the bodies had been washed away from the concrete portion of the canal. I would have to be a hundred per cent sure in order to give evidence to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So is the position this: You don't know how those bodies came to no longer be in the concrete section of the canal on the second day?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know. There had been a lot of rain. The level of the water in the canal rose during the night, and the bodies were washed away from the concrete portion of the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. That, so that we're clear, is your supposition?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's supposition, but it's also fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Let me move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The matter is clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me move on. You were shown yesterday by Mr. Dutertre a piece of video footage which showed a vehicle in the canal, the right-way up with its boot open, and the camera was shooting into the open boot. Do you remember seeing that piece of footage?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you identified that footage for us as having been taken on the 15th of September, which indeed is the date that appears upon it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you told us yesterday that it was on the 15th of September that the vehicle was turned from it roof on to it wheels; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We tried to recover the vehicles from the canyon with the help of the tow services. That's why the vehicle was moved. It was not found in the place where it was originally spotted, towards the middle of the canal. It was moved to the edges and it was turned so it was no longer upside down, but it was on its wheels.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that. And the turning operation you told us took place on the 15th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We have footage for the 12th and the 13th which shows the vehicle on its roof, which would seem to accord with your recollection that it must have been turned over either on the 15th; or if not then, then on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you can help us to this extent, there was no operation going on in the canal on the 14th, was there, because of the flow of water?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Recalling that piece of footage which you were shown yesterday of the open boot, could we please look at paragraph 64 of your witness statement. You say there that during your first visit it is possible that you saw the car in the canyon but didn't pay attention to it; and then in the last sentence of that paragraph, you say: "Later on, in the trunk of this car, a body of a woman was found. It later turned out that it was the car of the Frrokaj family, and that the woman was Ilira Frrokaj." Now, pausing there. How do you know that the body was found in the trunk of that car? Did you see that yourself?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw the body. The -- a leg could be seen protruding from the trunk, and the body was later on recovered and I tended to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So just to be clear, did you see the body in the boot of the car, in the trunk of the car, when it was opened?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And, presumably, that occurred after the car had been put on its wheels. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. While the car was still on the roof, we opened the trunk and the body just fell out of the trunk because the vehicle was upside down at that moment, and you have that on -- in one of the photos. You can see a body by the car, and that is also featured in video footage. The body just fell out of the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I don't think your memory is correct, Mr. Avramovic, that the body in the boot is featured in any of the photographs or in any of the video footage.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see it in the trunk, but you can see it by the car, on the ground, after it had fallen out of the trunk.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And Petar Ilincic, was he there when it was falling out of the trunk?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: With his camera?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to move on now, if I may, to ask you one or two questions about the Dashinoc site. Now, if we look at paragraphs 77 to 78 of your witness statement, you say there that your impression is that you went to the Dashinoc site on the 11th of September, that you have viewed the footage on that -- for that occasion, which also indicates the 11th of September. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if we look at tab 27 in the brown file, which I think is annex 20 to your witness statement, that is a plan showing the area around Dashinoc where that recovery occurred. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you compile that plan?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you just help us as to why it's dated the 10th of September?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already explained. This is tied to the book of on-site inspections. If the 9th was the first day, this should be on the 11th, and this is the error that has been tied to the whole situation, the error that just goes on repeating itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. That's what we're trying to understand. You're saying that the reason this says the 10th is because the entry in the book that records the first visit as the 8th must be an error. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if the entry in the book had been correct and had said the 9th, you would have put the 11th on this plan, which would correspond with the video. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that is yet another reason for you to believe that this visit did -- first visit cannot have taken place on the 8th. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. In the addendum to your consolidated witness statement, Mr. Avramovic, the first addendum, you deal with a number of sets of remains that were placed into the same coffin at Hotel Pashtrik, and you refer there to a photograph of the coffin and to the fact that it contained remains labelled D2, D3, R27, R33, and R35, all of which were interred into the same coffin. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Those five bags were put together. I just wanted to be clear, if you could help us. First of all, the "D" exhibits were retrieved from Dashinoc. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did anybody ever give you an explanation as to why remains that were found in Dashinoc were taken to the canal area rather than direct to Hotel Pashtrik?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because that was the base for investigations. This was something like our headquarters for the team. In order to save us the journey back to Djakovica every day, we set up our headquarters there throughout the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: These remains from Dashinoc were taken to the canal at the end of the day, were they not?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the investigation was over.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: On the day in question?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And by that stage, there was a mortuary in Hotel Pashtrik, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but it is possible that this was still not provided for.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Well, we'll hear other evidence about that. Did you transport these bones to the canal yourself?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire team, all of us who were present, we travelled in several vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the majority of the remains from the canal were removed on the 11th and taken to Hotel Pashtrik. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I wouldn't say that most of them were removed. I believe that this was done over a number of days, a few days at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: By the time you got back to the canal that evening, remains were already being taken to Hotel Pashtrik, were they not?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see where the witness said where he went back to the canal in the evening. He did not say this in the -- his witness statement after the operation in Dasinovac. I think this is not sufficiently precise. Could the question be reformulated or be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I put that from the evidence of Mr. Tomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but the witness gave a version in his own -- in his consolidated statement of the facts. And, perhaps, one should refer to what he says himself, and later maybe he can be interrogated about what the other witness says.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, let's be clear here. If Mr. Emmerson would refer to the witness's earlier testimony or statement, he should reflect that very precisely. If, however, Mr. Emmerson puts a leading question to the witness in which he suggests that something happened, then Mr. Emmerson is entitled to do that unless it comes down to pure speculation, having no reasonable foundation whatsoever. But if Mr. Emmerson refers to what another witness said earlier, just in factual terms, then he's entitled to do so. Of course, the next step might be that if there's any inconsistency, to put that inconsistency to the witness. But I think, as a matter of fact, that the question as such is not inadmissible. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear, was the bag of bones opened when it went back to the canal?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you think of any reason from what you were being told why the bag might have been opened at the canal?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Going back to the addendum to your consolidated witness statement, can you just help us, please, as to how it could come about that two bone samples from the Dashinoc site could have become separated from the remainder of the Dashinoc bones and buried into a coffin or put into a coffin along with three sets of remains from the Lake Radonjic site?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this question, Mr. President. The operations of post mortems themselves and the results of the doctors who made those choices and the autopsies they did, I don't think the witness can answer the question why certain remains from Dasinovac may have been put in this coffin with other remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, if the witness doesn't know, he's tell us. Whether he does know or not, it's certainly not something that he could under no circumstances know. So Mr. Emmerson is entitled to ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think, if I may say so, the witness purports to give an account of it in his witness statement in the addendum.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So just to be clear, Mr. Avramovic, you say in the addendum to your witness statement that these five different set of remains were put in the same coffin. Now, you'll probably recall that the families of Slobodan Radosevic and Milan Radunovic took away the bulk being of those remains of those two individuals, which were separately buried in coffins with their names on it. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you may or may not know this, but DNA analysis has established that the bones that went into this joint coffin included the bones of one of those two individuals. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You saw them being put into the same coffin. I just wanted to understand from you, if you can give us any explanation of what you saw, either at the canal or at Hotel Pashtrik, which could account for the fact that part of those two individuals had been put into a coffin with the remains of other individuals allegedly found at the canal?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't have an explanation, but you ought to put that question to the forensics themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It must follow, mustn't it, that at some point the bones from Dashinoc were separated?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Can we look at paragraph 181 now of your witness statement, where you refer to a series of further sets of remains that were recovered from various locations close to the economic farm later on in the month, you say about a week later. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if I put it to you that the date of that recovery is recorded in official documentation as the 23rd of September - and we've got the records in the yellow file, if you would wish to see them - are you in a position to confirm that that is correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a week from the end of the exhumation process, therefore, from the 16th. That's what I had in mind when I was giving the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. So that would take us exactly to the 23rd; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, pausing there, if you would. If you could just look behind tab 8 in the brown file, there is a note there of an interview between the Office of the Prosecutor and a man called Blerim Tahiraj. Blerim Tahiraj is the son of two individuals called Tush and Ramiz Tahiraj who were labelled as RE2 and RE3 in the recovery operation you indicate in paragraph 181. And if you would turn to paragraph 8 in that statement, you will see that the son of one of these -- I'm sorry, the son of this couple, RE2 and RE3, records that his parents were last seen alive when they left home from Skivjan on the 6th of September. Do you see that? Do you see that, paragraph 8?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the translation here.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understood you read English, Mr. Avramovic. Have I got that wrong? Do you not read English?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand quite well, but it's a bit more difficult with reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Let me read it to you, the relevant passage. On paragraph 8: "On the 6th of September, both my parents, Ramiz Tahiraj and Tush Tahiraj" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're reading, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll stop for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- "left from Skivjan about 11.00 a.m. by a red Lada car towards the direction of the village of Pozar." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I won't read the rest of that paragraph, except the sentence that reads: "They took the route from Skivjan through Novo Sello." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then paragraph 10: "After one or two weeks of their disappearance, one Serb, Moma Derlovic or Drelovic, who was a suspended policeman, told my brother, Valdet, on the phone that he checked prisons in Peje and Gjakove, and that my parents were in prison but their names were not made public." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you know a police officer or did you at the time by the name of Moma Derlovic or Drelovic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it's Momo Drljevic, a suspended police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So there is a suspended police officer by that name?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drljevic is his name. Momo Drljevic is his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And where was he stationed before he was suspended?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In the same building that you were working?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And what was he suspended for?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Some embezzlement or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you look at paragraph 12 now, the witness there tells the OTP that "we had heard these rumours that Serbs captured people in Novo Sello on the 6th of September, 1998," and then he says that on his way to Pozar on the 7th of September some people, mostly old ones, said the police and paramilitary were capturing people on the 6th of September. Did you know that there was an operation going on in Novo Sello on the 6th of September?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Avramovic, last week the Prosecution served upon the Defence a detailed forensic report by an international team of forensic analysts from France that reviewed the records and photographs in connection with these remains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object to the use of this report. In fact, the witness himself did not produce this report, which is an expert report, and I do not see how Mr. Avramovic could make any statement as regards an expert forensic report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We don't know yet what the question is Mr. Emmerson will put. Mr. Avramovic, Mr. Emmerson will now complete the question he started to put to you; but before you answer that, would you please pause for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Avramovic, the analysis of the remains of those two individuals by an independent forensic specialist team concluded that at the time of their discovery on the 23rd of May [sic], those remains had been dead for a maximum of 15 days and a minimum of eight days, which would place the date of their death at some point between the 8th and the 15th of September. My question is: You were present in and around the canal on a number of days between the 8th and the 15th of September, were you not?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 23rd of May causes me some --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, 23rd of September --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please pose the question so there can be no confusion whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, just to be clear. The independent analysis of those remains has concluded that at the time of their discovery on the 23rd of September, they had been dead for a maximum of 15 and a minimum of eight days, which would place their death at some point between the 8th and the 15th of September. Now, I just want to be clear. Those were the very dates that the Serbian team were operating in and around the canal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you turn now, please, to tab 9. This is a witness statement made by a man called Ahmet Maxhuni who is the father of an individual called Refik Maxhuni, who was body RE4 found during the course of that 23rd of September operation in the area around the economic farm. You can see, if you turn to paragraph 6 of his witness statement, he says: "My younger son Refik is dead. He was arrested by the Serbian police in 1998; and after that, I have never seen him again alive. Later in this statement, I will describe the circumstances of his arrest." In paragraph 14 he sayings: "On the 4th of September about 6.40 a.m., Refik left our apartment. He did not want to tell me where he is going. He just informed me that he should back soon. He took all the money he had, all 4.000 German marks with him. I advised him to leave the money at home, but he did not want to do it. "About ten or 15 minutes later, I looked through the window in my apartment's room. I noticed that my son Refik was stopped by the Serbian police patrol on Street Mother Teresa. "The distance from the place where he was stopped to the window of my apartment is about 70 metres. The window is coming out towards the direction of Hotel Pashtrik. I could easily see everything. My apartment is located on the fifth floor, and the visual at this morning was rather clear. "Looking through the window, I saw four Serbian police officers dressed in blue camouflage uniforms" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're reading, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- "Two of them had automatic guns and two had personal arms." If you could turn over to paragraphs 21 and 22: "I did not see if my son had been searched, neither if his hands had been tied. I noticed only that these policemen surrendered him and took him away in the direction of Piskote area, where the Serbian police check-point was situated. "At this moment, last time I have seen my son alive, I remember having very bad feeling that I could not see him again." Do you see those passages?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was able to see all that from that distance? Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, the independent forensic analysis has concluded that the remains of Refik Maxhuni, discovered on the 23rd of September, had been dead for a maximum of 15 and a minimum of eight days, Mr. Avramovic. Again, that is the period that you and your colleagues were present in the area around the canal; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would you turn now, please, behind tab 28. This is a witness statement to the Prosecution made by Vahdete Kuqi who is the wife of a man called Safet Kuqi, who is established by DNA to have been body RE6. If you could look at paragraph 3, as she described her husband in the last four lines, she says: "Although my brother, Sahedin Shehu, was a member of the KLA in Gllogjan and my husband was always a supporter of what my brother was doing, he never did anything to join. Of course, at that time, all the Albanians were supporters of the KLA. "On the 6th of September, 1998, my husband left the family home on a bicycle to go to the Zhdrelle, a village seven kilometres from Gjakove in the direction of Lake Radoniq." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you look at paragraph 6, you can see that the witness confirms that that was the last occasion on which she saw her husband alive. Do you see that, first sentence of paragraph 6?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now would you turn behind tab 29, where there is a witness statement made on the 5th of September --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the signed version is 29B, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- by a man called Skender Gllojani, who says in the third paragraph on the first page, that he has known Safet Kuqi since his childhood. Do you see that? This is on the first page, Mr. Avramovic, halfway down the first page he says: "I can say that I have known Safet Kuqi since my childhood." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And a little bit further down: "I am aware that Safet disappeared on one of the days early in September. I know that his wife Valdete spent a lot of time and effort to try to find out what happened to him." If we turn to page 2, please, he describes the incident on the occasion where he last saw him alive. Page 2, third paragraph: "We were walking towards the direction of Gjakove, when I saw that walking towards us was Safet. He was with his bicycle and alone. "As I got nearer, I saw a police car that was travelling along the same road coming towards us. It was a Zastava model of car. As I got to the point where Safet was stopped, two police officers got out. Both of them were in uniform. They stopped Safet, and I could see that they were talking to him. "I continued walking towards them. As I got closer, one of the police officers saw us and pointed his rifle at me. I saw that it was a sniper rifle. He said to me, as I drew nearer, words to the effect: 'Don't come back here. It's not allowed to walk in this area.' "I carried on walking with the others, but I saw that, as I was walking away, the other police officer with Safet was holding his driving licence. I saw him rip it up and throw it down. I did not have any chance to ask what they were doing with Safet. I saw Sindzelic pointing the rifle at Safet, guarding him, while Gojko began to beat him. "I could hear that the police officers were swearing at him and were saying the same things to him such as that he did not know -- such as that did he know that he was not allowed to walk around in that area. "I recognised the police officers. I knew them as 'Gojko' and 'Sindzelic.' I only recall these first names at the moment but others know who they are, and I will try to find out the other names. I recognised them as being police officers for a long time in the Gjakove area." Do those two names of police officers ring any bells for you,

utterances.speaker: MR. AVRAMOVIC
utterances.text: Gojko and Sindzelic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Sindzelic was the chief of the traffic police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Gojko?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably a traffic policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. "After this, I never saw Safet again; and to my knowledge, neither did anyone else. I know that the day I saw him was the last time he was seen. I know this from conversations with Valdete and the fact that the clothing he was wearing when I saw him was exactly the same as what he was wearing on the day he disappeared." Now, Mr. Avramovic, again, remains discovered on the 23rd of September; again, independent international forensic analysis is that they had been dead -- he had been dead for a minimum of eight days and a maximum of 15 days at the time of his recovery; and, again, those were the dates upon which you and your colleagues were in full control of the area around the canal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that we were in full control of the area. We were in the immediate vicinity of the canal of some 200 or 300 metres, and that was only for the time we spent there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm moving on to a new topic. I have two topics to cover. Would that be a convenient moment rather than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we have a break, I would like to briefly discuss the remaining issues of scheduling for today and tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, Mr. Avramovic, we'll discuss matters which are not directly related to you but related to the witnesses still to come. Therefore, the break starts already for you. Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Avramovic out of the courtroom. We'll see you back in approximately half an hour, Mr. Avramovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There has been some discussion on who would be the next witness. I think yesterday, at approximately 5.30, I was called by one of the Legal Officers, saying that the proposition that Professor Dunjic would be the next in line to testify was impossible because the documents -- numerous documents had not been uploaded yet. Then I see that the other witness, that is, Mr. Aleksandric - I think is Professor Aleksandric - was the one who would be available but might have difficulties to stay until Thursday, and, therefore, that was the reason, initially, preference was there for Professor Dunjic. Then yesterday, at 20 minutes past 6.00, I think that this message that the Chamber would, under those circumstances, prefer to hear evidence, and, therefore, if the material to be uploaded for Professor Dunjic was not uploaded, that we would then have to hear Professor Aleksandric. Now it was this morning that -- but if there has been any earlier communication, please tell me, Mr. Dutertre. It was this morning that I learned that the materials for Professor Dunjic were uploaded. That's information I think I received at quarter past 9.00 this morning, already in court, and that, therefore, the Prosecution would, despite the information of yesterday that it was not possible to hear the testimony of Professor Dunjic, nevertheless, would have Professor Dunjic as next in line. Is that correctly reflecting what happened, Mr. Dutertre?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The annexes regarding Professor Dunjic will be uploaded and available tomorrow. So the witness will be available tomorrow for the Chamber, if there is time to hear him. Indeed, Professor Aleksandric is available for examination-in-chief by the Prosecution, so the order would be Aleksandric first, if you agree; and then if time remains, Professor Dunjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll then I see that one of the problems also is that I do understand that Professor Aleksandric is not available for cross-examination until after the summer recess.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, he could stay until -- he could stay until tomorrow evening and then --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you ask Mr. Dutertre to repeat because he was interrupted by -- there were --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He would only be available after the summer break of the court otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. Now, my question to the interpreters: Is there still something missing, because -- or is everything now on the record? Mr. Dutertre, there was -- the English interpretation asked you to repeat the line where you started saying: "Well, he would stay until -- he could stay until tomorrow evening and then --"

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And then after tomorrow evening, he would only be available for cross-examination after the summer break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We know what the problems are to start the cross-examination of either of these two experts this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just in order to be fair to all parties to the Prosecution, if I can just indicate in two or three sentences, the chronology from yesterday afternoon. It was an occasion in which there was a round of telephone calls between Mr. Zahar, Mr. Re, and myself, in an effort to see how best to utilise the time. And, originally, it was thought that Mr. Aleksandric could not be here on Thursday, and that there was difficulty with uploading the exhibits for Professor Dunjic. So the object was to try to use the last part of today with Professor Dunjic, if possible, and then to call Professor Aleksandric so that his examination-in-chief and cross-examination could take place in one go after the summer recess, so that one doesn't have examination-in-chief this side of the summer recess and then a very long gap between that and cross-examination. But we're entirely in the Trial Chamber's hands, given that, as I understand it, we're all proceeding on the assumption that neither will be cross-examined this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since I take it the two experts are present here, the Chamber would like to hear as much of their evidence, even if that would mean that they could not be cross-examined any earlier than after the summer recess. We'll consider the matter over the break. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. Whichever witness is called to testify, issues concerning their 92 ter statements have yet to be resolved, although suggestions were made 24 hours ago, at least with Mr. Aleksandric, and we have yet to receive a response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The reason why I'm a bit concerned about these developments is that if overnight the information changes, is Dunjic uploaded, yes or not; of course, the materials uploaded; and then I do not know -- I do not know in the evening hours which 92 ter statement to take to read. I mean, I move from Aleksandric to Dunjic. We have expert reports filed on the 12th of January. For myself, but I take it the same for my colleagues, we would like not to be surprised at 9.00 in the morning that we might have looked at the wrong material. Therefore, if anything changes - and it's the second time that I'm now referring to late at night - if everything changes after 6.00, the parties are requested to inform the Legal Officer so that I can change the document in front of me, if need be, at 10.30 at night. Similarly, as I said before, the Chamber doesn't want to spend any time anymore on rather futile issues on which wording is still acceptable in a 92 ter, which is not. And if the parties, now having the experience how the Chamber approaches these matters, are not able to resolve them, I am firm that I want to be called at 10.00 at night or at 7.00 in the morning in order to resolve these matters rather than to spend time on it in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I, just for the sake of the next witness, I think the last communication that emanated from the Trial Chamber was to indicate that the next witness ought to be Professor Aleksandric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, on the assumption that -- on the assumption that the material for Professor Dunjic was not uploaded. So from the information I now received that uploading the material for Professor Dunjic will not be ready this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We still have an option to hear perhaps, but we'll consider that, the testimony of Professor Dunjic tomorrow, the testimony in chief. Now the times scheduled. Professor Aleksandric was three and a half hours. Is that correctly understood? Professor Dunjic was for one hour, one hour and a half?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Approximately that, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the next question, Mr. Emmerson, Mr. Guy-Smith, and Mr. Harvey: How much time would we still need with Mr. Avramovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So far as I'm concerned, 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Forty-five minutes. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have the sneaking suspicion I will be very short, based upon my conversation with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I may be even shorter than Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is the negative minutes. You gain time rather than to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's usually a good thing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- lose time. Yes. Unfortunately, we can't go back in time. So, therefore, the Chamber can be confident that Mr. Avramovic will conclude his testimony in the next session. We'll consider then how to proceed. We have a break until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, before we proceed, I understood from the questions you objected against the use of a certain report, which just by hearing seems to be exculpatory in its nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, a recent report has been received and some information has been used in an exculpatory manner by the Defence, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I think it was only one week ago that I reminded the Prosecution of their duty that disclosure that arrives late is not only to be disclosed to the other party but to the Chamber as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I will have to check, but I believe this document has been given to the Defence before you had made that reminder, but we will apply it a posteriori.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. You have to apply the rules is what we expect you to do and not a posteriori. So, when reminded that this statement taken in January from a witness has to be disclosed to the Chamber as well, because it's late disclosure, I think what the OTP should have done at that moment was to go through the files and see whether there was any, let me say, non-routine disclosure which could have an impact on the case, and disclose it immediately to the Chamber as well because that's what the Rules tell you to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I must tell you that this is something that the Prosecution received very recently. It's not as if it were something that were already in the system and that had not been disclosed. We received it recently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if you receive it and if there's a reason to disclose it, late disclosure should also be disclosed to the Chamber. That's what the Rules tell you. I'm not blaming you for not having been in a position to do it any earlier. I mean, if you receive it, of course, you can't do it any earlier. But the Rules say if you receive such material late and if you disclose it at a late stage, then you should disclose it to the Chamber as well. That's the simple message I give to the OTP at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I provided to the Trial Chamber a copy of the report. Without going into the detail of the contents at this stage, I mentioned certain matters in relation to the RE bodies. Your Honours will see the terms of the instructions that went to the experts; and in particular, they were asked to give an accurate estimation of the date of death and to give an estimation by reference to the appearance of the remains in situ, as to how long they had been in situ. And there are on a body-by-body bases analysis of those matters, and they are collated together in tables and conclusions at the end. Suffice it to say for these purposes that the estimation is that the remains found adjacent to the canal wall are of some considerable age, either one or, one to two, or two, or three, or more than three months, but that the conclusion of the forensic experts is that they had been in situ, each of them, for a very short period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Just for my information, then we'll continue. This report has been made on the request of whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was the Prosecution, and the Prosecution intends to present a motion to that effect soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that information, Mr. Dutertre. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Avramovic, could you please turn to paragraph 15 of your witness statement. You there refer to a map upon which you have marked the main Gjakove to Peje road and an area you've marked in yellow which you describe as an area which was "unsafe for Serbs." Is that correct, "unsafe for Serbs" is what you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And: "... and the police to go, unless they wanted to be killed. It was unsafe for the police to travel to these areas until they were liberated in September 1998. The police did not travel there. They just used the Djakovica-Decan-Peje main road, which was the only road which could be used, although it was still very dangerous." Do you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me be clear what your evidence is in this regard. It is your evidence that there was no police operations conducted in the areas to the west and east of the main Peje to Gjakove road prior to September?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry. Is that the testimony you are giving in paragraph 15 of your witness statement, that the police never went into the territory that you've marked on that map?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. They never went in depth of that territory, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. I'm going to suggest to you that that's simply not true, and that you know full well that the paramilitary police were frequently conducting operations in those areas throughout the period from April to September.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that there was a substantial VJ battalion stationed in the area of Lake Radoniq from February to September?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could Mr. Emmerson make his question a bit more precise when he refers to the area of Lake Radonjic. It's somewhat vague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have pointed earlier at some confusion about zones, areas, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So for the witness to know precisely what the question is, you should be more precise. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There were VJ forces stationed to the west and south of Lake Radoniq, immediately adjacent to it, from February to September is the suggestion.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, but it was to the south, next to the dam by the lake; and as for the area to the west, I wouldn't know. I don't think that this is correct, that this is true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: West and south is something perhaps to be clarified. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, specifically, that there was Serb forces on the summit of Suka Bitesh during this period?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It is possible. Well, let's look if we can briefly at policing operations. Could you turn behind tab 33 for the moment in the brown?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the one just provided, and I don't know whether it is inserted.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It is inserted. It was disclosed to the Defence last night.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the tab number.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Tab number 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, this, Mr. Avramovic, is a report, a regular combat report, of the 125th Motorised Brigade command, that is a VJ brigade based in Peje, dated the 30th of April. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 1 refers to information available on the 29th of April and says this: "According to the information available, on the 29th of April, the MUP forces from the Klina village searched a part of the terrain in the Iglarevo village, and they had found nothing." And then it goes on: "The Decan-Pezar-Jablanica road is controlled by the terrorists at the exit from Decan. In the course of the day, two dead bodies were found on the said road near the Dasinovac village that the terrorists had kidnapped and killed some time ago." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, pausing there for a moment, it's clear there, is it not, therefore, that at the end of April, there were MUP forces in the area around Dasinovac?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ah, it is possible, at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The beginning is possible but not later on. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So, by the end of April, do you accept that there may well have been MUP forces in that area?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, MUP forces are not mentioned here. The only thing that is mentioned are VJ forces in Iglarevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The first line of paragraph 1 refers to MUP forces. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the territory mentioned is the territory of Klina, which does not belong to the municipality of Djakovica. This is the Pec-Klina-Iglarevo road area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Can you help me about this: What do you know about two bodies having been found in the area of Dasinovac as early as the end of April?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you anything. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That would have been reported to the area for which you were responsible, would it not?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if we were sent to the site. But it is also possible that no on-site inspection was carried out; and for that reason, I'm not familiar with the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we, with that in mind, please, turn to tab 24 in the bundle --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- just for my understanding, I do understand that Pezar is the same as Pozar.
