utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's my assumption as well; and if you look in the original, it looks as though it may well have been Pozar rather than Pezar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the report says two dead bodies were found on this road. It doesn't say by whom. Is there any reason to follow your suggestion that it was found during an operation by this brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm just looking.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- it's a matter for textual analysis in paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So, as I understand the witness's testimony, he accepts that by the end of April, the MUP were or may have been entering those areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, we've heard testimony, Mr. Avramovic, from a senior RDB official in this court, that there were regular operations being conducted by the MUP into that territory, once or twice a week, during the period from the 1st of July. Can you help us with that at all?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This may have been the case along the road, but not in depth of the territory in my view. I'm not sure. I'm not familiar with all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Because the evidence that we have heard from Mr. Bajcetic is that operations and clashes were taking place even in the area of the canal where the bodies were found between the 1st of July and the 8th of September.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Could you then behind tab 24 look at paragraph 3.9. Tab 24, as you can see, is a Pristina Corps command document dated the 18th of August and signed by commander Colonel-General Nebojsa Pavkovic. At paragraph 3.9 --

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please repeat the tab number.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Tab number 24?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So, for the 18th of August, there is an instruction at 3.9 to: "Withdraw the 52nd Bomber Regiment from Radonjicko Jezero to the Kosovski Junaci barracks and transfer the positions to MUP forces." Do you see that? Do you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it does not specify the part of the lake, any part of the lake.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I understand that. It indicates, does it not, that: "The forces from the battalion in the old barracks in Gjakove, the strength of one company, are to be on standby." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was there a transfer of MUP forces into the area around the lake in August, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to object to this question, which is vague, again, referring to the area around the lake in August. We don't know exactly where we're referring to, and we don't know what the date is either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, whenever you are talking about the area around the lake or the canal area, I would like you to define it as precisely as possible, because earlier you referred to another witness who I think described the operations to take place in certain villages, which you then now summarized as in a certain area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You pointed to that, and, therefore, I would prefer you then to refer to this testimony as another witness said that in such "villages as."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that may be close to the canal area, but let's not, as a natural inclination, to expand or to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I respond to this because it's an objection that keeps being raised in different forms. Two dimensions to it. The proposition that I put to the witness in relation to the evidence of Mr. Bajcetic arose out of the specific question and answer given in re-examination in which he was asked: Were these clashes taking place in the specific area in which the bodies were recovered at the end of the concrete section of the canal? And he confirmed that they were. So one can't really get much more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So far as the material concerning the deployment of forces around the lake is concerned, I can go only on what the material in front of me says. And the material here in front of me refers to stationing the positions at Radonjic Lake and reinforcing them by replacing the 52nd Bomber unit with the MUP. Now, I can't put a more specific proposition than that which is revealed upon the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Obviously, if the witness is in a position to say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that. If he knows something about it --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Then we can ask a supplementary question for him to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn to tab 31, please, Mr. Avramovic. This is a slightly earlier order, dated the 8th of August. Again, it's an order of the 125th Motorised Brigade, and it's signed by commander Colonel Dragan Zivanovic. Do you see paragraphs 2.6 and 2.7? "BG-52 with reinforcements shall support the attack of the main forces of MUP 2nd Detachment, Pristina CPJP," that is special police units company, "and the SAJ on the axis of Radonjicka Suka to Saptej to Rznic, and with part of its forces shall participate in coordinated action on the axis of Donji Bites village to Gramocelj to Saptej village." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this is just a plan. It doesn't mean that the operation actually took place during that particular period of time, as far as I can tell from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just bear with me, Mr. Avramovic, because we've all watched a videotape in this court, twice now, which shows paramilitary police officers taking control of Gllogjan and Irzniq on the 11th. So before you make comments such as that, please, forebear, I'm simply asking you at this stage to confirm what we see in the documents. Paragraph 2.7: "BG 549-3 shall support the attack of p/s of the MUP 9th Detachment and the Prizren CPJP on the axis of Erec village, Erecka Suma, Babaloc village, and Rastavica village." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So, at least, Mr. Avramovic, we can agree that on the 8th of August, there was a plan for coordinated action for the MUP - that is to say, the PJP - and the SAJ to engage in military action from Radonjicka Suka - that is to say, Suka Bitesh, the hill immediately to the west of Lake Radoniq - towards Shaptej and Irzniq; and also on an axis from Donji Bites village - which is to the west of the lake, as I'm sure you remember - towards Gramaqel and Shaptej. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And a similar operation from Erecka Suma towards Babaloc and Rastavica. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, as I said a moment ago, we in this courtroom - and we can play it for you, if you it would help you, but I think it would simply take up time at this stage - have watched footage of paramilitary police taking control of Gllogjan and Irzniq on the 11th and 12th of August. It is your evidence that you were unaware that there was a major offensive taking place at that time, involving the MUP, the SAJ, the PJP, and the VJ?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. I wasn't aware of the locations mentioned herein.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Were you aware that there was a major coordinated attack between the VJ, the SAJ, and the PJP in the area to the east of the main road towards Gllogjan and Irzniq at the beginning of August? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't, not at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were you aware of it when you signed a witness statement, saying the police never travelled off the main road before September, were you aware of it then?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you weren't then aware of it before you came into the witness box. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So how were you in a position to sign a witness statement saying that the police never travelled off the main road, Mr. Avramovic, if you don't know one way or the other what's going on on the ground? Why did you put that in your witness statement?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my statement, and that's the knowledge I had or I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You don't say in your statement: "I have no knowledge one way or the other." You make a categorical assertion for something that is palpably false. Now, can you explain to us how that comes about?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There may have been an error in interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. What about the end-of-May period, Mr. Avramovic, were you aware that there was a major joint VJ and MUP operation in the areas of Streoc and Lybeniq, for example, in which --

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That borders with the territory of the municipality of Pec, or rather, I believe it falls under that municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask clarification for one question. Mr. Avramovic, Mr. Emmerson told you about the footage shown to this Chamber of paramilitary police taking control of Gllogjan and Rznic on the 11th and 12th of August, and then he asked you whether you were unaware of a major offensive taking place at that time. And your answer was: "It is. I wasn't aware of the locations mentioned herein," which was not entirely clear to me. Did you mean to say you were aware of this operation, but not where it took place? Or did you mean to say that you did not even know about these locations to exist, or where to find them? What was exactly meant by this answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, there was a great deal of fighting along the road itself. I did not know about them reaching that location; namely, Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear to me now. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn behind tab 22, please, for a moment, and if you could look at the second paragraph. This is a record of observations by the team from the British Military Attache's office in Belgrade on the 11th and 12th of May in the Ponosevac area. Do you see the first paragraph refers to: "The area of Ponosevac, Djakovica, Pec, and Decani being patrolled by elements of the JSO and PJP in a very heavy-handed way. Villagers have fled north to Junik." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 2 in relation to Ponosevac: "Road from south to Ponosevac 'carpeted' in empty cases, including 40-millimetre grenades. Villages south of Ponosevac deserted, livestock slaughtered in fields, houses sprayed with gun-fire. Ponosevac empty except for JSO/PJP, who are carrying out patrols from Decani using APCs," and various other types of equipment are recorded. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you aware of those operations being conducted in the early part of May in the Ponosevac area?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew that there was fighting around Ponosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were you aware of the fact that Serbian forces had forced the civilian population out of Ponosevac, killing their livestock and burning their houses?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object about this question. The witness is a crime scene technician, a policeman. He is not part of units taking part to fights. I don't think he is a specialist of these matters, and I don't think he can answer all these detailed questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm testing the assertion of his witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you aware that the tactics used by the MUP forces included forcing the civilian population out, burning their houses, and killing their livestock?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Have you never come across, in your time in Djakovica as a police technician, information that the MUP and PJP forces were engaged in house-burning operations?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably there were individual cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. But you don't accept that it was a policy?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know of any such policy, if there was one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, we've heard evidence from the British Military Attache, who attended the canal on the 8th of September, that there were houses in the area still on fire and 300 joint PJP and VJ forces engaged in levelling villages, such as Prilep, to the ground so that they were standing at only 30 centimetres high. Is that something that you were unaware of in September, Mr. Avramovic? Is that something you were unaware of?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was fierce fighting going on in Prilep.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn behind tab 32 for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, could you just help me out. Ponosevac, I usually have no difficulties in quickly finding.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: To the west of the main road south of Junik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: South of Junik. I'll find it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if we could look behind tab 32, can you find page 5, for a moment, please, in that selection. This is an interview or a record of an interview conducted by the Office of the Prosecutor in July 1999 with a man called Ersad Colovic, who, as you can see under the heading "military service," was assigned to the 3rd Army Pristina Corps 549th Brigade on the 8th of June 1998. And he explains the name of his operation; that is to say, 1st Motorised Platoon, 3rd Squad, stationed in Djakovica barracks. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: With three commanders there recorded: Commander Milan Markovic, the squad commander; Lieutenant Rade Radojevic, the platoon commander. Do you know that name at all?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were most probably members of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me see if I can prompt your recollection. Mr. Radojevic was convicted of murdering civilians on the 16th of September of 2002. Does that prompt your recollection?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You weren't aware that one of the commanders who was stationed near to the lake, as this man was, was subsequently convicted of murdering Albanian civilians?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. And then a company commander called Janos Sel. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Major Janos Sel. Now, If we can pick it up, please, at page 9, under the heading -- do you see the heading at the bottom of page 9: "Killings in the villages." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So under that heading, if you could just turn to page 10, just halfway down the page, if you can see a sentence that begins: "We operated in the Radojicko Jerzero area. We first operated around Silman-Baka and Babaj Boks areas and then headed north-east towards Radojicko Jezero." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, but, again, it does not state which reach of the lake exactly, because Babaj Boks is on the opposite side, facing the border with Albania. And Lake Radonjic is to the north-east with Babaj Boks. That is the north-east section of Lake Radonjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so. We will come to the precise locations in just a moment. Be patient. What the witness is there telling the OTP is that he headed from Babaj Boks north-east to Radojicko Jezero, and you say that would take you to the northern end of the lake. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the eastern or south-eastern reach of it, on the dam.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Carry on on page 11. "From Siman, we started moving north-east towards Radonjicko lake. We were walking. We spent time around the lake until late August." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "Between Siman and Radonjicko, we went around two other villages. They were populated villages. "At the lake area, we attacked a number of villages: Raskoc, Rakoc," and although it says "Donja Brits," in geographical terms that must, I think, be Donji Bites and Gornji Bites. Do you see those two references there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know where Rakoc and Raskoc are, don't you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the northern side of the lake, in the direction of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat the name of the location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the name of the location you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Raskoc and Rakoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We can see them on our map on the northern tip of the lake, just on the eastern side, I think. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether the witness can tell us what we see on the map, he has nothing from Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put it to him in words, rather than take time with the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They are on the northern tip of the lake on the eastern side. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Close to the area where the canal joins the lake, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's on the opposite side of the lake. It's not that close, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me read on, because he then describes the other areas. Donji Bites and Gornji Bites, they are on the western side of the lake, are they?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, in fact, you went through one of those villages on the occasion that you visited on either the 8th or the 9th. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let's just pick it up, if we can, just halfway down the page. "Most of the people killed were killed in their yards while they were trying to flee. We used to use anti-tank anti-armour launchers into houses. This killed a lot of people. Orders were to kill people in their yards or in front of their houses. Not everyone was killed. One group we would get orders to kill everyone, so we would kill everyone. With other groups, we would be under orders not to kill, so we would let them all go. The Major made these orders and the 2nd Lieutenant sometimes, mostly the Major. "The largest group of persons killed that I am aware was ten persons (women and children). This happened in Gornji Bites. It was in August. We entered the village. We were under orders. We found the group, and we were under orders to kill them, so we did. "In 70 per cent of the villages we entered, the major would rape at least one woman." And then he describes some further details in relation to that. He then says: "The women were in their 30s and 40s, men in their 50s, and two children about 12 or 13 years old. They were all killed by rifle. They were killed in a group. They were moving in a group in one of the side streets. That's where they were shot. No one lived. They all died. They were all executed. They were shot at by two squads who received orders to kill. One of those squads was my squad. Here one could avoid shooting in the people because of the distance if they want. The Major could not control who was shooting where." He then says this: "We stayed in the area that night. The next morning the bodies were gone. "The Major was always near us during the attack because we were positioned near the centre of the attacks being the 3rd Squad. There were maybe five or six other men killed that day besides these ten, but those are the ones I saw. This was a large village. "The dead bodies would not be there the next morning. They were collected by the militia." And then he refers over the page to leaving the lake area in mid-September. Now, as a crime scene investigator, Mr. Avramovic, were you aware in mid-August of there having been a killing of a large number of people in Gornji Bites by Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that. Had I been aware of it, probably a crime scene investigation would have been conducted, but these were members of the VJ of the Yugoslav Army. They did not inform the police force of their actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So, if it's true that the bodies were cleared up afterwards by the militia, can you just help us as to what the word "militia" might refer to in this context?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps the military police, perhaps the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. But none of this was information that ever came through to you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was there a practice of moving bodies, as far as you were aware, after killings in the villages in order to cover-up the Serb crimes?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You are aware, of course, of the large numbers of bodies transported to Serbia and recovered in the mass graves in Batajnica?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You told us, yesterday, that Lieutenant-Colonel Vlastimir Djordjevic you thought may have attended the canal scene on the first day. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. I don't remember, though. There were quite a few dignitaries. There was a crowd of people there on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I have one final topic I want to ask you questions about, and it concerns the ballistics parts of your evidence. I can do this briefly. Could you please turn --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Behind tab 32, we find in English two interviews --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- not real statements, and we now and then find references to times so that's something happened for about 20 days or --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it happened in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But to find the proper time-frame causes me quite some difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I can indicate how Your Honour can work that out in relation to this particular statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The witness was assigned to the 3rd Army Pristina Corps on the 8th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we, I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Under the heading "military service."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you turn to page 12, he indicates that he deserted as a result of these crimes on the 15th of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So, when he refers to August and September, he must be referring to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean there's only one August in that period --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and one September? Mr. Dutertre, if you could assist me further, apart from August and 20 days, I'm just trying to orient myself since it's been put to the witness, and I'd like to fully understand what exactly it is that is put to the witness. If there's nothing to add, Mr. Dutertre, then Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It is, in fact --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, nothing to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It is, in fact, possible to trace through the witness's account of the time and to be clear, at least to the extent he is referring, to a period in July and August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's possible.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The Prosecution is asked to switch off the mike.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I won't take a lot of time on it at the moment, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. The matter has been sufficiently clarified for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn, please, to Exhibit 66 to your witness statement, which ought to be in the black file of exhibits. This is the document you have produced concerning ballistics analyses. Do you have that? No. This is -- you won't find it in the yellow file. You had it in front of you yesterday. That was the file of exhibits that was produced by yourself attached to your witness statement, and I'm looking at annex 66.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters have not been provided with the black file.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. In which case, I shall read very slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just check to make sure we're looking at the right document. Does the document that you have upon it, does it have a number at the top left U0164231? Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if you look at the third paragraph beginning on the 24th of March, and then if you could please look at the second sentence in that paragraph, it reads, in the English, as follows. I'll just read it slowly. "In the ballistics expert report 03 number 234-1-216/98, the expert concluded the following: ..." And this is, I'm told, the exhibit, for the sake of the record, which is P448. "The casings sent for analysis had been fired from ten different fire-arms, and the casings were identical to," and then there are three bullet points. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know what has happened to the ballistics report that you refer to there under the number 234-1-216/98?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report exists in the Djakovica SUP and is part of the file, the original I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's not part of the papers that you've handed over or exhibited to your witness statement, is it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When did you last see that report?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two years ago, and it does exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perhaps we may get to see it in due course, but can I ask you, please, about these bullet points. First of all, this is you summarizing what was in that report, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You say in the first bullet point: "29 casings," that is, 29 casings which were allegedly found in Gllogjan on the 24th of March, "29 casings were identical to 29 casings found at the scene of the terrorist attack on the house of Stevan Maslovaric, in the village of Pljancor on the 7th of March." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you can drop down two bullet points, it also says, "29 casings were identical to eight casings found during the crime scene investigation into a terrorist attack on the house of Stevan Maslovaric, in the village of Pljancor on the 7th of March." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The other 28 casings or 29, if I recall well, because quite a few casings were found at the scene of crime. 158 in total were found there as a result of that visit attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So can I be clear, is it a coincidence then that 29 in the first group match 29, and 29 in the second group match eight?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: AK-47 rifle uses cartridge magazines of 30 bullets each, and there's always one bullet less in it, so that there would be no jamming. So it is the common practice with some soldiers to take one bullet out, in order to prevent the jamming of the rifle, and that's the AK-47 rifle or the Kalashnikov, which has 30 bullets in each of those magazines. That's why it's mentioned here as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know if the 29 casings in the first example are the same or different from the 29 casings in the second example?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe they're different.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And what do you base that on, Mr. Avramovic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was written based on the expert's report; in other words, this is just - how shall I put it? - this is just an overview of the cases of terrorist attacks that were somehow connected.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And so far as the second part of your record is concerned, in relation to the recovery of casings from the canal, the indication is that 24 casings were identical to 29 casings found at the attack on the house of Stevan Maslovaric, near the village of Pljancor. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not 24, this was a typing error. It should read 14, instead of 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. It should read 14, but, in fact, it was typed with, I think, a "2" and a "1" at different times. Do you know whether the 29 casings, that 14 are said to have been identical to, were the first or the second of the two 29 casings that are referred to in the first part of the group of bullet points?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, when it refers then to the 29 casings found during the crime scene investigation in Gllogjan, do you know if that is a reference to the first 29 said to have been found at Stevan Mas -- at Gllogjan and to have been connected to the ones found at Stevan Maslovaric's house, or the second 29 that you say are different?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. I can't say anything with any precision. I should have to consult the report. Maybe the expert did not specify anything. When we send our reports, we say exactly the number of casings and he didn't do that. All these casings should bear a marking on all of them, and he never specified any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you don't know, from your own records, whether the comparison is with individual markings identifying it as an individual weapon or with a kind of weapon with you, do you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One individual weapon, based on the findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And on what do you base that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is based on -- on the ballistic report.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I won't take you to it, but the ballistics report doesn't say that, Mr. Avramovic.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When a ballistics expert says that the casings are identical, that means that they were fired from one rifle, not from two similar rifles. When it says "identical," then it means that they were fired from one and the same rifle, because every rifle has its particular characteristics. So when a ballistics expert says "identical," he means just one individual rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you ever have an opportunity to study the basis for those conclusions?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the proceedings because I went through the ballistics training that had to do with the identification of casings and rifles from which the bullets were fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: My question was: Did you ever have an opportunity to study the basis for the conclusions in the report that you have considered?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't have that opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, finally, this: Paragraph 187 of your statement contains the following two sentences, and you are referring here to the report of

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: "The report did not specify which casings matched with the casings found at the crime scene. The ballistics report did not specify the casings." What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the request that we forwarded to the ballistics expert, together with the casings, you will see that we have described exactly under what numbers were what casings fired, but he ignored that. For example, there was number 1, 20 casings; number 2, 30 casings. But the in his response, he did not replicate our request.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: His report refers to casings found in Gramaqel, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what you can find in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you have transposed that in your exhibit 66 to Gllogjan, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because that investigation is filed under the name Glodjane. I don't know how he came by his data. It's the same case, Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You say it's the same case. You didn't see the documents from which he was working, did you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was working on the basis of our request that we forwarded, together with the casings. There may have been an error in the request. Maybe it says "Gramocelj," but I'm not sure. I don't have it on me. I can't consult. I can't check.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How do you know what it was that he was comparing? How are you in a position to say he was comparing the Gllogjan rather than the Gramaqel, when your request was simply to compare the Lake Radoniq canal casings with any casings that they had on file? How do you know?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every piece of mail that is dispatched is recorded under name. Every document is tied to that number in order to avoid any possible misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the 03 number that you have on top of every document.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Just to be clear so that we all understand, the request that you sent to Mr. Visnjic to conduct comparisons was a request to conduct a comparison between the 117 cartridges found and any cartridges deposited in a collection in Pristina. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with a collection of cartridges that were tied to the terrorist attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you don't know which ones he is comparing them with, do you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably the entire collection.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So, when he's making the connection with Gramaqel, on what basis do you say he meant to say Gllogjan? What basis have you for making that assertion?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the number under which it was recorded, the 03 plus the date of the event. There were very few events taking place on the same date. On that particular day, there was just one terrorist attack, and there could have been no confusion about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, just pause with me for a moment, if you would, please, because there is no number, is there - perhaps you can help me - on the expert's report which enables you to see which file he was comparing it with, is there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a number as part of the heading, which is relative to our number, the number of our request.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's the number of your request, and you've told us your request was to compare the canal casings with any casings in collection; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is there any number in Captain Visnjic's report which connects to the casings allegedly seized in Gllogjan, any number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to be certain that the witness has the appropriate report in front of him because this had been excluded. I want to be absolutely certain he has the proper text in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. It's Exhibit 63, I believe. Yes, annex 63 is the report and annex 62 is the request.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just have a look at that quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could a -- perhaps a hard copy of both of these documents. 62 is not excluded, I think, 63 is. I leave it -- it was upon your --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- request, at least Defence request, to exclude 63. For these purposes, you would like to withdraw that?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm not withdrawing it. It's just that in order to understand the witness's testimony ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, if you look at Exhibit 62, that's your request, is it not?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that doesn't make any specific reference, does it, to the Gllogjan file?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to Radonjic lake and Dasinovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it asks the experts to compare the casings to all casings in the collection; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, then if you turn to annex 63, there is the report which we can see reaches a conclusion about Gramaqel on the 24th of March. And you told us a moment ago that you could connect that with Gllogjan because of a reference number in the report. Could you tell us, please, what reference number in the report you're there referring to?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the report the date is what matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it's the date --

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date of the terrorist attack. I thought there would be a reference number, but I could not be sure of that before I actually consulted the document. On that day there was just one terrorist attack, just one on-site investigation. There could have been no confusion about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So let's be clear. You withdraw the testimony indicating that there is a reference number. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there was a number, but you're right, it's not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: On the 24th of March, there was a substantial operation in which Serb forces, including special forces, entered into Gllogjan through Gramaqel. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was from several directions, but I don't know. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so. There was fighting all over the area on the 24th of March, including in Irzniq and surrounding villages, was there not?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How do you know that the comparison here being made is with specific casings seized in Gllogjan rather than Gramaqel?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were the only body authorised to send casings for ballistics analysis; in other words, what my colleagues found in Glodjane was sent for analysis. There were no other casings. We were the only ones to send requests for ballistics analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you there when they were found?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but my colleagues were.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you have any record available of where they were found, those particular casings?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there must be sketches here on the file.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We'll look to see if there is a reference to the specific cartridges in issue. Finally this: You say in your addendum, addendum number 2, that the reason you can make a connection is because the Haradinaj family home is located near the border between Gllogjan and Gramaqel. There is no border, Mr. Avramovic, between Gllogjan and Gramaqel. Between Gllogjan and Gramaqel are the villages of Dubrave and Shaptej. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Saptej is somewhat to the north and Dubrava is in between. There's no border. This is a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. The Haradinaj family home is close to the border between the municipalities of Gllogjan and of Dubrave; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that should be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so Gramaqel is some considerable distance further on?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two or three kilometres maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I'm looking at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm so sorry. I've concluded with my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, as much as I would like to sally forth, I don't wish to cover a ground that has been covered, and, therefore, I have no questions of this witness at this time. I'm satisfied --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- with the state of the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, still less time needed than Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Dutertre, any need to put further questions? I already can tell you that the Chamber for very practical reasons has to adjourn four minutes from now. How much time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Approximately ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I suggest that we have the break now, and we'll have a break for 20 minutes. And may I remind the parties that very often already halfway the Chamber fully understands what the issue is and whether there's any formal border or whether there's a village in between, the Chamber by now can know these details. And, of course, to put questions to the witness with the certainty that sometimes there is no logical answer to be given, the Chamber sometimes has a preview or a feeling that that would be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the parties would please keep that in mind for the remainder of the examination. We'll have a break for 20 minutes. We'll resume at 20 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Avramovic, yesterday you indicated that you had seen a number of individuals who had been arrested on September 3rd in your office, and that you saw part of those people the first time you went to the lake. My question is as follows: When you saw those individuals who had been arrested again, did you notice any signs that they had been beaten on these individuals?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And, more generally, did you notice any other signs of poor treatment?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could only see that they were tired.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'd like to go on to another topic which relates to the issue of the dates of your first visit to the lake. You indicated that you thought that the first visit took place on September 9th, in particular you indicated that this was on the basis of documents that you consulted later on, that you saw later on, and you mentioned in particular a document which was a document by -- made by the investigating magistrate. My first question relating to that is as follows: Did that investigating magistrate, or rather, was that investigating magistrate present the first time you went to the lake?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not present. It was only on the following day, on the 10th, that he arrived on the site for the first time. I'm talking about September 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'd like to refer to paragraph 106 of your witness statement, in particular a request made by Judge Gojkovic dated September 9th, 1998. This is annex 26 of your consolidated statement. My question is as follows, if you would be so kind as to answer: Do you know whether or not the judge wrote the text before he himself went to the lake, that is, when he found out about it; or after he went to the lake, having seen the actual site; or later on?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he did it based on the information that we collected on site. The team reported back to him, and I believe that the document was drafted based on that, before he came to the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'd like to go on to the third item. On page 11 of the transcript, this morning's transcript, Mr. Emmerson asked you the following question, and I shall read it out in English: [In English] "It's perfectly possible for Serbian officials to get to the canal area from Donji Bites. Is that right." And your answer was: "Yes." [Interpretation] I would like to ask you to clarify that answer. When you say "yes," do you mean that it was possible to go to the canal from Donji Bites on that particular day, that is, when you went to the lake for your first visit; or are you referring to the previous period, that is, the period before this visit, that in general it was possible for the Serb forces to go to the canal before that date?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I said only that day. It was not possible on any of the previous days. On that day, this was the only safe road to the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Another issue, Mr. Avramovic, which is still related to the canal, however. When you arrived at the canal the first day, were there other members of the police or Serb officers there? Did they arrive in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They arrived after us. They were the first ones to arrive, the investigating team and security. The other teams arrived after us, but I don't know when.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would like to go on to something completely different. You indicated that you participated in the recovery of the bodies that were discovered on September 23rd, 1998. My first question on this topic is as follows: Between the date of your first visit and the 16th, when you indicated that the recovery of bodies, that is, the first series of bodies, the recovery had been completed. So, again, I -- between the first day and the 16th, did you go to the precise places where the bodies were subsequently found on September 23rd, 1998?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't go. It was a very large area to search. That's why all the bodies were not found immediately there. Bodies were concealed. Some branches and twigs were strewn all over them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have an additional question on this same topic. On the 23rd, was this the first time that you saw those bodies?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to go on to one last point. You indicated that on March 24th, 1998, when Mr. Otovic, the police officer, was killed, that was the only incident that occurred on that day, in the territory that we're referring to around Gllogjan. Can you tell the Court whether or not there were police investigations carried out on that day?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may have been some events, but the only case about which an investigation was carried out was that event in Glodjane and that particular terrorist attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to refer to paragraph 188 of your consolidated statement as well as annex 64. I'm particularly interested, Mr. Avramovic, in two documents whose ERN numbers are as follows -- in fact, there are two. It's document U002-5418 up to U002-5422. My question, Mr. Avramovic, is: Is this document a document that results from the investigation carried out in March -- March 24th, 1998, following the event that took place in Otovic, the Otovic event?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Let me locate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Fine, take your time.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For information, it's 64 [as interpreted] ter 1465.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I will put my question differently. Is this document the result of an investigation carried out following the death of Mr. Otovic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to take a look at page 4 of this document, which is a sketch. Both in the Serb and English-language versions, there is a word that is "key" or "legend." [In English] "... with cartridge cases beside the window in which fire was opened in the direction of the patrol." [Interpretation] Can you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not just one casing. There were several.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, is that the page of what you said there are translations now but the Chamber has not yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I do have some additional copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are exactly the -- that was, of course, the concern of the Chamber where it had no agenda, when it asked for full translations. So additional copies, I would say, the Chamber is the first one to get copies here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it's on page 4 in the English-language translation. Your Honour, this is my last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: The casings that are mentioned in this sketch, are they the casings that were collected during the investigation carried out following the death of Mr. Otovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, before the witness answers that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: My understanding is that this witness was not present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre, I think the first matter that should be clarified as to whether the witness is the author or whether he personally attended when these casings were found.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Avramovic, were you -- were you personally present when this investigation was carried out?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't, but I know a colleague of mine who was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What is the name of that colleague?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Veselin Nesovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Avramovic, how can you know then that the casings mentioned on this sketch were the casings collected by Mr. Nesovic, the colleague you mentioned, or one or other of the individuals who were present?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were the casings he brought over from that scene of crime as part of the standard procedure, and I know this because there were no other casings found and there were no other scenes of crime attended on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Avramovic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one point, if I may. The corrected version of the consolidated statement is now in the e-court system, and I would like to request the -- I would like to tender both the document and the annexes in evidence, as well as all of the annexes for which exhibit numbers I believe have already been given meanwhile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it with the exception of 63 again. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We haven't, in fact, seen the amended version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then I take it that if the amendments are made properly, that we'll then hear from you. Any further --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one or more questions to you, Mr. Avramovic, but let me just ... Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that you recently reviewed the entries in the crime scene register. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now where exactly - I think you gave us the place where they were stored - was that in?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Djakovica SUP, in Jagodina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, are all the materials stored in Jagodina in relation to this case, or just this crime scene register?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that we were involved in doing. Original photographs, original photo album photographs, the negatives, all of that is kept in Jagodina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the casings you sent in ...?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The casings were sent to the SUP in Pristina and were kept there because of the collection that they were keeping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then another question is: Were ever any bullets sent in for comparison in relation to, as you called them, terrorist cases?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that they were, but I don't recall whether they existed in relation to this particular case. If there were some found at the scene of crime, then they must have been sent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you're personally not aware of any bullets being seized, well, let's say, at the Lake Radonjic canal, the concrete part?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that bullets were found in the bodies during autopsies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you know what happened with those bullets?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA AVRAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Then, Mr. Avramovic, this concludes your evidence. I'd like to thank you for coming to The Hague and for answering all the questions that have been put to you. I wish you a safe trip home again. Madam Usher, would you please escort Mr. Avramovic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, has a list already been prepared in relation to the previous and this witness in view --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm very sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I usually switch to 5 if I want to hear French. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The answer is that there is a work in progress as we speak, both in relation to Mr. Bajcetic and in relation to Mr. Avramovic, and we will be in a position to provide the details to Madam Registrar by the end of the morning today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I take it also to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Dutertre or Mr. Re, you're both present. Your next witness would be Professor Aleksandric, as far as I understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. Professor Aleksandric is the next witness. He's here, available to testify now. Ms. Issa will lead that witness through his evidence, Mr. Dutertre, and I will be in the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But Ms. Issa is not. Oh, you're hidden. Ms. Issa, I should have not said this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It's no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I couldn't see you from here. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There's been a discussions between the parties about redactions to the Rule 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They have not all been agreed. What we propose from this side of the bar is that Your Honours have the Rule 92 ter statement; it be marked for identification; the discussions continue, objections be taken to testimony as it is elicited orally; and then, if it is necessary, at the end of the testimony to seek the Trial Chamber's ruling on any particular passage, that come be done prior to this a decision on admission. Is that acceptable to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, Is that acceptable to you for the time being

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: As a provisional measure, yes. I sent a letter, I think, to the Trial Chamber and to the parties setting out the eight areas of disagreement remaining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll proceed on this basis. Then, this morning, I said at a certain moment that I thought Mr. Dunjic also was a professor. I usually do not use titles if it's in relation to experts, so I hardly call anyone "general" or "minister" or anything like that. I think, however, calling someone as "professor," if he appears as an expert in the field in which he is a professor, that is different. This is just to explain my approach of this matter. Is Professor Aleksandric nearby, Madam Usher? Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: While he's coming in, I perhaps could assist the Trial Chamber on his way in. Ms. Issa has prepared or we have had prepared a binder in relation to -- a photograph album for the Trial Chamber's assistance and that of the Defence of the photographs which we will show the witness during his examination-in-chief. That could be distributed now. In relation to his 92 ter statement, there are a number of proposed attachments and exhibits. A chart has been drawn setting out the proposed exhibit number in one column, with a 65 ter number in the other. We had to put a virtual number on what we anticipated was going to be the next number available in the court. So, assuming we are up to P456 and it's still current, this is the proposed list of exhibits for the witness, and if that can be distributed to the Defence and to the Trial Chamber, which I have been has been circulated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think we have seen such a list. It has been informally communicated already to the Chamber's staff. There's, of course, one pending issue. We now slowly moved from 94 bis to 92 ter. Are we receiving all the evidence through the 92 ter statement with attachments, with additional testimony in court? Or should we still decide the -- I think there were four statements that were filed on the 12th of January, if I do not make any mistake, that were then presented as expert reports under 94 bis.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We originally, yes, did file a proposed statement under Rule 94 bis as a proposed expert report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I doubt there's any disagreement from the Defence Professor Aleksandric is a qualified expert; however, in the circumstances, we simply propose to lead what would normally be an expert report by 92 ter, lead some oral evidence, and have him cross-examined in the end. You actually come to the same result in the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, therefore, only the 92 ter statement finally will contain the whole of the evidence the Prosecution wants to present in relation to Professor Aleksandric --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of course, with all the attachments?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the 94 bis, 12th of January, has been dealt with. This raises some other questions since Professor Aleksandric has not yet entered the courtroom. Is there any challenge to Professor Aleksandric being an expert? I mean, this is not whether you would agree with all the methods he has used, but just whether he qualifies as an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There's no disagreement that he qualifies as an expert. There may be some disagreement as to the extent of his expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Mr. Harvey, same position as far --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I take the same position, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, I noted that earlier you were on your feet, and then once I gave priority to someone else you --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Perfectly fine. And it was taken care of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Thank you. Ms. Issa, the Chamber would very much like to deal with the two expert witnesses before the end of tomorrow's hearing. So, if you would please keep that in mind, there will only be examination-in-chief at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Professor Aleksandric.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphones are not switched on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Professor Aleksandric, before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Professor Aleksandric. Please be seated. You'll first be examined by Ms. Issa, who's counsel for the Prosecution. And I take it that she has explained to you that the Chamber already received a lengthy statement in which you give already quite extensive report on your activities. So please be aware that the Chamber is aware of that. Ms. Issa, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Dr. Aleksandric. Dr. Aleksandric.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I'm listening to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Just to -- just for the record, Dr. Aleksandric, would you please state your full name.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: Branimir Aleksandric; father's name Vitomir.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And your date of birth is what?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 21st of September, 1949, in Belgrade, Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And, just very briefly, sir, you're presently a professor and director of forensic medicine the Institute of Forensic Medicine at the University of Belgrade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You are also a professor of forensic medicine at the faculty of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, let's be very practical. This is paragraph 1 of the --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- statement of Professor Aleksandric. Professor Aleksandric, in your statement, you've listed your present positions, a lot. The Chamber is aware of that. Please proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps, sir, I can just ask you a couple of quick questions just in brief. Can you indicate how many crime scenes you've attended over the course of your career, that's not contained in your statement?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: In my career, it was not part of my job to attend scene crimes -- crime scenes. However, in my 30-odd years of career and experience, I would join the police force to attend crime scenes of certain murders in Belgrade. As far as mass graves are concerned, this was the first time I worked on that, save for Batajnica in 2002. I also have some experience in exhuming bodies in Bosnia in the course of the war there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, Professor Aleksandric, during the course of -- during the week of June 11, 2007, you gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you've reviewed that statement in the Serbian language, which is your language, is that right, to make sure that it's accurate?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you signed that statement and found it to be accurate. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that the witness be shown P456, Exhibit P456.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is, Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sorry. That's the 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Has a number been assigned? By whom? That is good cooperation between the registry --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It has, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's great.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since it's not the final version yet, it doesn't make that much of a difference whether it's shown through Sanction or whether Madam Registrar should show it. Yes. I've on my screen now a curriculum vitae.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's the wrong exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the wrong one? I don't know who -- I take it that comes from the Prosecution, then if you could show us the right one.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We've got it now in front of ourselves. What's your question, Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's your statement and your signature, is that correct, Dr. Aleksandric?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: I can't make out any of this. I can't see it properly, but whatever I signed, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If you can just look at the very bottom of the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a possibility to zoom-in or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, there is. We're just about to do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. [Interpretation] Yes, those are my initials. Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that the witness be permitted to have a hard copy of his statement to refer to it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: -- as he goes along in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May a hard copy be provided to Professor Aleksandric. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. I'd like to just tender the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa, the Rules require two matters to be tested: The first one to be whether it reflects what he said, the second is - I didn't invent the Rule - that whether the witness would give the same answers if the same questions would be put to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, if you would, please, seek that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, after that you reviewed you statement, you've now indicated that that is your signature. Does that statement reflect what you would say in court today if you were asked about the same matters?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. A decision on admission will be -- will be given at a later stage when the matters of any redactions have been settled. Please proceed, Ms. Issa. But the document is now marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Your Honour, perhaps to save time just at the outset, I would like to indicate I would be tendering all the exhibits at the end of Dr. Aleksandric's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Dr. Aleksandric, you refer to, in paragraph 7-8 of your statement, receiving a request from the investigative Judge Gojkovic from the Pec district court during September 1998; and in paragraph 9 of your statement, you say that you were assigned to a team to investigate the crime scene. Can you just indicate how did you first learn of the bodies at the Lake Radonjic canal?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: The request from investigating judge was dated the 9th of September, and I believe it was received by the institute on the 10th of September.
