It was a request addressing the institute to assign a team that would go down into the field, inspect the site, to recover the bodies, and perform autopsies of any remains found. In the course of the 10th, we, the colleagues, agreed amongst us who would go and Snezana Veljkovic, the head of our department, officially accompanied this team. And this document bears the date of either the 10th or the 11th of September. Professor Dunjic and I, my colleague Jecmenica, and Radivoje Krajisnik were assigned that team.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And in paragraph 12 of your statement, you say that you arrived at the Lake Radonjic canal area on 11 September. Did you see any bodies upon arriving?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: When we arrived in the area next to the canal, we immediately saw several corpses lying on the ground. These were the bodies that we were able to see in that patch of grass. Most of the bodies were covered by earth and only parts of their bodies were visible.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Turning then to Exhibit P452, if you can look at your screen and just explain what were your first observations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, perhaps this is an exhibit -- witnesses comment on what they see, therefore, it should be perfectly clear, either on the basis of the running numbers at the bottom or by the correct or not correct dates and times indicated on the videotape, what the witness was looking at and to what he comments. So could you please then say start at this time or start at 4.30.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because otherwise it's totally impossible later to know what the witness actually saw. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I think it started around 4.40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we restart it now. I don't think it did at 4.40 because it is now at 4.42, that's 2 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we could then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Restart --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: -- restart the portion, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It starts at 3.55, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. What begins at 3.35? It says here 11.22. I don't understand what starts at 3.35. I'm not with you. You've lost me. It says --.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- on the footage, the date is 11 of September and the time is 11.22 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksandric, there is a counter a little bit further down, red numbers. It has been established by now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay, okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- It has been established by now that at least the time - I'm not saying anything more - the time being, I think, somewhere in the middle of the night might not be correct. Therefore, this is just administrative matters we'll be able to handle. Just concentrate on what you see and answer the questions in relation to that. Could we go back to 3.55 or 3.56.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we could just go to the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the left wall of the concrete man-made canal. Its interior side leads to the water-flow show many signs of damage, of bullet damage. This is the plateau next to the right exterior wall, and here the camera zooms-in on the place where the group of bodies were found, either on the surface of the ground or very close to it. This is the video footage that the cameraman did before we started marking the bodies. This is just a general view of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. And did you meet anyone when you first arrived at the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, the video stops at 4.42. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you meet anyone when you first arrived at the scene?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were lots of police officers there who secured the area and the general area. There was a lorry, ready to transport the bodies. There was also a tent that had been put up for logistics purposes. This is the tent where we used to eat in or take our refreshments during the breaks.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, but what I would like you to explain is that you indicate in paragraph 12 of your statement that you met with the Serbian police who were already at the scene, and then you say that: "The police found the bodies about two days before we arrived at the scene." Can you indicate how you knew that the police found the bodies two days before you arrived at the scene?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: The conclusion was simple. If we arrived there on the 11th and Judge Gojkovic's document was dated the 9th, that's two days. But also we heard that two days before our arrival the bodies were found. So based on those two things, I drew my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Who did you hear this from?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: From Judge Gojkovic and from the police officers who were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you also say in paragraph 13 that immediately after you arrived at Lake Radonjic you then went to the Ekonomija farm. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: Correct. When we arrived and when we took stock of that part of the canal, immediately after that, the police took us to the Ekonomija because a body had been found there as well. So they wanted us to inspect that place as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: How far is the Ekonomija farm to the canal?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: In my free estimate, as you go down the road, it's 300 metres. We were taken there by a lorry -- actually, by an off-road vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When you arrived at the Ekonomija farm, can you just briefly describe what you saw there?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: The police showed us the place where the body had been found. It was a canal; and in that canal which was covered with mobile plates, a body was found, a body of a man. We marked the body immediately, we recovered it, we put it on the lorry, and we returned to the original canal since the police did not find any other bodies at the Ekonomija.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just to clarify, when you refer to "it was a canal," in paragraph 54 of your statement, you say that at the Ekonomija farm, one body was found indeed the drainage canal. And that's what you're referring to; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you also describe in that same paragraph, 54, that the crime scene was marked at the site RE1, then photographed and filmed. You just indicated you marked the body. Can you indicate -- can you just explain briefly why you marked it with RE1?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: As we arrived at the Ekonomija where the police had found one body, we marked it as "RE" which stood for place Rznic, that's R, and "E" stands for Ekonomija, and number "1" stands for body number 1. This was the code that we agreed on immediately, and the bodies that would be found 300 metres from there by the canal would be marked with letter R standing for Rznic, and then we would use numbers in sequence to mark every subsequent body, in order to make a distinction between the site called Ekonomija and the site at the canal or at along the canal. That's why we used two different markings.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And in paragraph 55 of your statement, you describe the farm as having two large rooms, stables for livestock with an automatic watering trough, and that there were seven electrical cables covered with plastic isolation, separately with dead knots to a horizontal medal rod, near seven watering troughs for livestock. Can you indicate what was the significance of finding those cables?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think Your Honour will anticipate the objection to that question and the nature of opinion evidence it is seeking to elicit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, is it clear to you what the objection is?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, not entirely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think it is that -- I take it, Mr. Emmerson, that you would consider the expertise of this witness to be mainly in the field of forensic medicine and not in forensic science in general.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The objection is that it is not for -- within the competence of this witness to be expressing opinions as to what he thought might be the purpose, which is I think the object of the question, for which items of cabling that he saw when he attended may have been put there or how they got the there or what they were for.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's not the object of the question; sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then perhaps you put the question in such a way that there's no confusion. I take it that we would rather first go through the facts as far as wire is concerned, and then -- at least that's how it is presented. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you -- I've just indicated a description that you have in your statement as to this cable. Can you provide us with any further description of the cable that was found at the farm?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: Those were electrical cables that are normally used in construction for electricity. Those cables were somewhat stronger, the size of a finger. I don't know any technical specifications of these cable. At one end they were closely and firmly tied to a bar above the trough, and on the other end they showed a very clean cut. There were seven of them, and we found some burned newspapers at the level of the area where the cables were cut. Later on by a body that we marked as R-8 near the canal, we found a segment of an identical cable.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you find this cable anywhere else in your processing of any other crime scene or similar cable anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. I believe that it was found only by body number 8 or by some other body. In any case, you can consult my daily report to be sure of the number of the body by which it was found.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, when you say it was found by some other body, what other body are you referring to? Where was that other body located?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: I said that I believe that this was by the body marked as R-8, which was found next to the concrete part of the canal, a body that was among the first group. I believe it was body R-8, but I'm not sure so you shouldn't hold me to it. In any case, I concluded that answer by saying that you can make sure about the number of body by which the cable was found if you consult my daily report.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll get do that at some point, but I would like to turn to Exhibit P609. Can you look at your screen?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is the transversal bar, and here you can see a policeman holding the free end of the cable, whose other end is firmly tied to that bar by a very special type of knot that we refer to as dead knot.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And that was taken at the -- that depicts the farm. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the Ekonomija, the farm.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You also mentioned that some burnt papers were found underneath the places where the cables were found, were tied. Did you -- what made you take notice of that?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC
utterances.text: We searched the area very broadly, and we made note of any detail that might prove to be of interest for a forensic investigation. And we did not find the burned papers anywhere else along the transfer bar but the places where the cables were tied. That's what made it so interesting.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was there any other -- was it significant to you for any other reason?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, I think it's plain where Ms. Issa is going with this. She's seeking in different forms of question to elicit opinion evidence, which is the subject of an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We do not know yet what she's seeking. Whether it was significant to you for any other reason, then, of course, we will hear whether it was and for what reason. And if that would amount to any opinion evidence which is not within the field of expertise of the witness, we'll then -- I take it then --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think, if I may say so, the witness has given -- I'm not going to press the objection, but the witness has given a description of the circumstances in which this material was found and supplementary question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree. Ms. Issa, you see that there's some concern about drawing conclusions which might not be in the direct field of expertise of this witness. Could you please keep that in the back of your mind when putting the questions to the witness, because if you make them too vague then, of course, there is a risk that that evidence comes to us. On the other hand, as may be clear to you, this is an expert witness. He can give opinion evidence; but, of course, if there would be any trace of any opinion which is not inside what we expect to be his field of expertise, then, of, course we would need a further foundation for that. And then we can decide whether such opinion is or is not within his field of expertise. At the same time, Mr. Emmerson, you also -- you can develop some expertise, even if you would ask a general expert in forensic science, they sometimes develop some additional expertise on matters closely related to that. If we would find such expertise, then, of course, we would have to explore on what it is based and how this expertise was gained. So, therefore, let's try not to work on the square millimetre and square centimetre when a field of hectares would be enough. I'm looking at the clock, Ms. Issa. Professor Aleksandric, we stop at a quarter to 2.00. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn, Professor Aleksandric, until tomorrow, 9.00, in this same courtroom. Could I already invite Madam Usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've forgotten. One second, one second. You understand, one second. I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak to anyone about your testimony, the testimony you have given up till now, or the testimony still to be given tomorrow. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that. You shouldn't worry. [In English] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it's my duty to tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, I noticed that quite a portion of the evidence you elicited from the witness clearly appears in his 92 ter statement. Would you perhaps give it some additional thought overnight how to focus on those matters that really need further explanation so that we finally will be able to finish the two expert witnesses tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will. It was just a matter of getting some context at the start, but I will certainly bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We stand adjourned until 9.00 tomorrow, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
